raw_response:
I am still going to plant cotton on all 10.9 mu. I have done this many years, and at my age I do not want to toss around with too many changes. Cotton is slower money than grain, but I know how to manage it, and this land suits it. We only have two people in the house, so I have to keep the work in a way we can handle ourselves. I cannot spend too much cash at the start, so I will use the usual local seed I trust, put on a base fertilizer first, then watch the crop. If the cotton grows weak, I add a bit more later. If it looks fine, I do not push too hard. Too much fertilizer costs money and can make the plants too lush.

For water, I have the well, but pumping costs money, so I will not irrigate blindly. If spring is dry after planting, I will give one water to help emergence. Later I will look at the ground and the leaves. In a normal year I think two waters are enough, maybe three if summer is very dry. For pests, cotton cannot be ignored. If I see aphids or bollworm, I will spray. Weeds also have to be controlled early, otherwise later it is too laborious for us old people. I will do ordinary rotary tillage before planting, because there is no need to make things complicated on this small area. I am not chasing the highest yield, just a steady crop that we can afford to raise.
